previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for dyspnea, chest heaviness, and productive cough due to acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. He presented with weight gain, bibasilar crackles, and mild pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. He was treated with IV furosemide, resulting in improved symptoms and a weight reduction from 135.3 kg to 127.3 kg. His troponin elevation was attributed to heart strain and chronic kidney disease. He remained on home heart failure medications, with ranitidine switched to pantoprazole for GERD symptoms. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weights, follow a low-salt diet, and complete outpatient labs and follow-up, including a repeat CT for a pulmonary nodule and a sleep study for suspected OSA.

# Congestive Heart Failure Exacerbation: Investigation of the 
etiology behind this exacerbation demonstrated that he had 
difficulty obtaining these medications secondary to insurer and 
provider ___.  He was admitted for diuresis and begun on 
a lasix infusion at 10mg/hr. Early in his course, he had 
multiple episodes of symptomatic, sustained VT that 
spontaneously resolved.  These episodes became less frequent 
with continued diuresis and was suspected to be secondary to 
fluid overloaded state.  Diuresis was continued to a final 
discharge dry weight of 130.8kg.  Although above his prior 
discharge weight, the patient refused on multiple occasions for 
a diagnostic right heart catheterization.  Walking around halls 
without dyspnea prior to his discharge and was able to sleep in 
his bed, symptomatically demonstrating improvement.  Improvement 
of BNP to 925 from 4197.  He was discharged on his home 
torsemide dosages of 80mg QAM and 40mg QPM. He was arranged 
follow up with a ___ affiliated cardiologist as well as a PCP.

# Asymptomatic sustained VT: Throughout his hospitalization, he 
had multiple ___ beat runs of VT, with the longest episode 
lasting 90seconds. All episodes were asymptomatic and 
spontaneously resolved without intervention. EP was consulted 
and adjusted his ICD settings.  In addition, his metoprolol, 
initially held in the setting of acute congestive heart failure 
exacerbation, was uptitrated to metoprolol 12.5mg PO q6h.  This 
was then converted to metoprolol 50mg daily on ___. Of 
note, he was on metoprolol succinate 150mg daily as an 
outpatient and may need uptitration as an outpatient. 
 
# DM type II: Stable throughout hospitalization. Coverage with 
ISS and continue lantus 50u at night.
 
#  Acute on chronic kidney disease: Bump in creatinine to 2.4 on 
___ with a suspected baseline creatinine of 1.4-1.7. Bump 
likely ___ overdiuresis. Diuresis was held for one day with 
improvement of creatinine and he was restarted on his home 
torsemide as described above.

disease with LCx totally occluded s/p DES and RCA with a distal 
60% lesion from last catheterization in ___. Mildly elevated 
troponins up to 0.03 on admission, secondary to CKD as past

aspirin, plavix, atorvastatin, imdur, hydalazine, with the up 
titration of hydralazine to 20mg TID greater reduction in 
afterload.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr ___,

You were recently hospitalized at the ___ 
___ for congestive heart failure exacerbation, or the 
build up of fluid in your body due to decreased functioning of 
your heart. We suspect that this was because you had not been 
taking your medications for the days to weeks prior to your 
admission.  We treated you with a medication called lasix, which 
helps to remove excess water from your body. We have made a few 
adjustments to your medications. You should stop taking your 
spironolactone.  You should also take an increased dosage of 
your hydralazine to 20mg three times a day.  In addtion, you 
should also take metoprolol 50mg daily. 

Please follow up with your new cardiologist, Dr. ___ 
at your appointment scheduled on ___ at 1:40PM.  Also 
please continue to take your medications.  If you are having 
difficulty getting these medications or run out, please call 
your doctor's office immediately.

In addition, we have arranged follow up with your primary care 
office on ___ at 11:30AM.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

It was a pleasure taking care of you. We wish you a happy and 
healthy Thanksgiving.
Your ___ cardiology team
